sense: of a shop or a museum
also: open (of a shop or a museum)
what time does the shop open?

terms.gloss: shut, closed (of a shop, a door)
evidence: Liv. 4.31: jūstitium in forō tabernaeque clausae
terms.comment: Livy’s shops are shut, clausae, and opened again, aperīrī, like doors. Cicero has occlūsīs tabernīs in the same sense (Cat. 4.17).

terms.gloss: be open (to visitors, of a building or a collection)
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.5: omnibus haec ad vīsendum patēbant cotīdiē
terms.comment: What stands open for people to come in and look, as the statues in a private house at Messana did every day. We have found no ancient phrase for “opening hours”; say it with patēre: Quibus hōrīs patet?

phrases.latin: Hodiē taberna clausa est; crās aperiētur.
phrases.english: The shop is closed today; it’ll open tomorrow.
When does the museum open? — At nine.
What are the museum’s opening hours?

phrases.latin: ubi patentēs jānuās et tabernīs apertīs prōposita omnia in mediō vīdit
phrases.english: when he saw the doors open and, with the shops open, all their wares set out in public

phrases.latin: Messānam ut quisque nostrum vēnerat, haec vīsere solēbat; omnibus haec ad vīsendum patēbant cotīdiē.
phrases.english: Any of us who came to Messana used to go and see these; they were open to everyone to see every day.
What time do you open? — At eight.

sources: Lewis & Short: claudo · Lewis & Short: aperio · Lewis & Short: pateo · Lewis & Short: occludo
